basics.name: Silvia Téliz
basics.label: PhD Candidate at the Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
basics.summary: I am a PhD candidate (expected July 2027) at the Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania, studying visual political communication and social biases in multimodal AI systems. I combine computer vision, natural language processing, and machine learning to analyze large-scale multimodal data, from TikTok content, to street political advertisements. My dissertation project, Visual Cues as Political Communication: A Computational Look into Mexican Federal Electoral Campaigns, examines how skin tone and other visual cues influence electoral outcomes in Mexico. I have also conducted research on the nature of social biases in large language models and visual language models. My work has been published in the International Journal of Press/Politics and presented at conferences such as IC2S2 and PolNet-PACSS. I have extensive experience in teaching and mentoring students, having served as a teaching fellow for two courses at the Annenberg School for Communication, and as an instructor of record at Universidad Panamericana.

work.name: Politics, Identities, and Communication Lab - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
highlights: Secured $10,000 USD via the Annenberg School for Communication Internal Grant for the project 'Identifying Biases in VLMs' Zero-Shot Classifications of Race and Gender' (2026-2027 academic year), as lead researcher.

Collaborated on the theoretical conceptualization, formulation of overarching research goals, methodology design, computational analysis of text and image data, writing, reviewing, and editing for projects developed within the lab under Dr. Deen Freelon's supervision.

work.name: Introduction to Communication Behavior - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
highlights: Taught lecture 'Media Effects on Community and Everyday Culture'.
Taught recitation section, providing students with additional support and guidance on course materials.
Tutored students on how to improve their studying strategies and reading comprehension skills for weekly exams. Provided guidance on the development of a research plan for their final projects.

work.name: Center for Advanced Research in Global Communication - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
highlights: Collaborated with Dr. Juan Llamas Rodríguez on the development of a mixed-methods study on the representation of gender and skin color stereotypes in Mexican telenovelas and TV series (a report commissioned by the Luminate foundation).

work.name: Children and Media - Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
highlights: Taught lecture 'Racial Representations in Children's Media'.
Clarified students' doubts and provided additional support on course materials during dedicated office hours.

work.name: Quantitative Methods for Communication Research - Universidad Panamericana
highlights: Taught introductory course on quantitative research methods for students in the Communication major.
Introduced R into the curriculum as the main tool for learning Quantitative Methods.
Guided students through in-class exercises, which included statistical analysis, data visualization, and interpretation of results using R.
Designed original educational materials, including slides, assignments, tests, and lab activities.

work.name: Facultad Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales (FLACSO)
highlights: Coordinated a research consulting project to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the evaluation system of information transparency for the National Institute of Access to Information and Personal Data Protection.

Developed an academic program and created didactic content for the National School for Women of the Institutional Revolutionary Party, empowering female members through education on gender perspective, political representation, and communication strategies.
Created educational content for the Migrant-e project (led by the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México), teaching undocumented immigrants in the United States about their rights and safety tools.
